anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard extension used to format this dataset, not a paper describing this alphabetic decision task dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded during an alphabetic decision task. The data were converted to BIDS with MNE-BIDS and custom code that joins behavioural data, stimulus information, and metadata. A channel wiring swap (FT7 and FC3) was corrected during conversion. Two interrupted recordings for sub-01 were concatenated with a boundary event, and recording dates were anonymised by a constant shift.

citation_details.title: Temporal dynamics of letter processing revealed by multivariate pattern analysis of EEG data
citation_details.author: Miguel Domingues, Susana Araújo, Tânia Fernandes, Inês Bramão
citation_details.abstract: • Single letter recognition relies on a cascade of continuous orthographic processes • This cascade begins when letter-specific processing emerges in the N1 time-window • Late evaluation processes, indexed by the P3, are part of this cascaded processing • Perceptual letter representations remain active during abstract orthographic stages • Early letter representations are reshaped, suggesting interactive processing stages Letters are the primitives of reading expertise. Single letter recognition relies on a hierarchy of processing stages, in which early visual features gradually evolve into abstract letter representations, but the temporal organization of these stages remains poorly understood. citation_details.title: Character Iconicity vs. Arbitrariness: An Arabic NLP Perspective
citation_details.author: Dorieh M. Alomari, Irfan Ahmad, Maged Saeed Al-shaibani
citation_details.abstract: Arabic script uses 28 letters, many of which share a common base shape (rasm) and are distinguished only by dot placement. Because early Arabic manuscripts were written without dots yet remained interpretable, dot removal offers a natural test of whether these visual distinctions are functionally necessary. Prior work has shown that dotless Arabic can remain readable and effective for natural language processing (NLP), but it remains unclear whether this success depends on preserving the original rasm groupings or whether arbitrary but consistent remappings to the same reduced rasm set can achieve comparable performance. We address this question by comparing standard dotted and dotless Arabic with arbitrary character remappings constrained to the same 19 undotted rasms. We generated 2,000 random remappings under word- and character-level tokenization and selected four representative mappings with the highest and lowest entropy values.
